correctness.rationale: For every \(n\ge2\) and \(1\le i\le n\), exposing the first \(i\) images leaves \(n-i\) directed paths whose uniformly random reconnection adds an expected \(H_{n-i}\) further cycles. Counting prescribed completed cycles and their joint upper-record probabilities yields \(\operatorname{Cov}(C_n,I_{n,i})=(i-1)/(i^2\binom ni)\). The \(k=i\) term and the fixed point at \(i\) are treated explicitly. The aggregate and its asymptotics follow from a binomial-denominator tail bound and classical Stirling marginals. The verifier independently checked 2472 exact assertions through nine symbols and all exposed-prefix conditional identities through six; finite tests do not substitute for the universal proof.

value.rationale: The exact positive dependence between cycle count and individual record-position events distinguishes joint behavior from classical Foata equidistribution. The nonuniform position profile concentrates the global covariance at the terminal record, while the full-count correlation is asymptotic to \(1/(n\log n)\). This is a motivated all-size structural identity for two central permutation observables, rather than an arbitrary finite slice or a statement about marginals alone.
